title: Terminal
idea: Give the in-game script editor a new pixel-art Terminal look that follows assets/ui/terminal/terminal-ref.aseprite (issue 4).

glossary.meaning: The in-game script editor with its new look; it edits the same npc scripts as today.
assets/ui/terminal/terminal-ref.aseprite: the panel mock-up on the left and a parts sheet on the right.
The dark bar along the top of the panel, above the tab bar, with the red button in its left corner.
The grey row under the top strip holding the tabs, the - button and the + button, with a light band under it.
One numbered line of the script area (00:, 01:), one glyph tall plus half the gap a 4 reference pixel row leaves, with nothing drawn between rows.
The SDL debug font the editor on main draws with today.
A 3 pixel light track along the right or bottom edge of the script area, with a 1 pixel grey thumb; shown only when the content overflows.

features.name: Panel
features.whatItDoes: Draws the Terminal frame: top strip, tab bar, light band and white script area.
details: Saved and parse error messages show in the top strip, as light text.
Uses the largest whole-number scale that fits inside 80% of the window, centered.
With no tabs open, shows blank rows with only the red and + buttons; typing does nothing.
Starts at 128x96 reference pixels, and any edge or corner can be dragged to resize it, between 64x40 reference pixels and the screen; the size is kept across close and open.
Dragging the dark top strip moves the panel, which stays fully on screen; its place is kept across close and open.

features.name: Tabs
features.whatItDoes: One tab per npc script, with a distinct active and inactive look.
details: Tabs widen to fit their names, and squeeze down when the bar fills up.

features.name: Red button
features.whatItDoes: Red square in the left corner of the top strip; closes the Terminal, same as Esc.
details: Bright at rest, dim while hovered, with a darker center pixel in both.

features.name: - button
features.whatItDoes: Closes the currently selected file; drawn right after the selected tab.
details: Closes the tab only; the file stays on disk and its tab returns the next time the Terminal opens.
Unsaved edits stay in memory and are back when the tab returns.
White at rest, light grey while hovered.

features.name: + button
features.whatItDoes: Creates a new script; drawn right after the last tab.
details: Opens a new tab with an editable name; Enter creates the .txt file, Esc cancels.
White at rest, light grey while hovered.

features.name: Numbered rows
features.whatItDoes: Shows script lines with two-digit numbers.
details: Text uses the original font.
Text scales separately from the art, so a row holds about 45 characters.
Plain text is black; other syntax colors are unchanged for now.
As many rows as fit show; the wheel and the cursor scroll through longer scripts.
A space between words is half a character wide; indent spaces at the start of a line stay full width.

features.name: Scrollbars
features.whatItDoes: Scroll the script up and down and long lines sideways.
details: Hidden until the lines or the longest line no longer fit.
A thumb's length follows the share of the script on screen, so it resizes as the file grows.
The wheel scrolls, a thumb can be dragged, and clicking a track jumps there.

features.name: Autocomplete list
features.whatItDoes: Shows suggestions for the word being typed, in the Terminal's look.
details: A 1 pixel navy edge and a white body.
Suggestions keep their syntax colors; the picked row sits on light grey.

features.name: Terminal button
features.whatItDoes: An icon button on the game screen that opens the Terminal when clicked.
details: Uses assets/ui/icon/terminal-icon.png, scaled by a whole number.
Its top sits 25% down the screen, 12 points from the left edge.
Drawn over the map and under the Terminal; a click on it never reaches the map.

flows.name: Edit and save a script
steps: Press Shift+1; the Terminal opens with one tab per script.
Click a tab, or the rows, to place the cursor, and type.
Save with Ctrl or Cmd+S; saved or the parse error shows in the top strip.
Click the red button or press Esc to close.

flows.name: Create a new script
steps: Click +; a new tab appears with an editable name.
Type the name and press Enter; the .txt file is created.
Or press Esc to cancel, and no file is made.

flows.name: Close a tab
steps: Select a tab; the - button sits right after it.
Click -; the tab closes, the file stays on disk, and unsaved edits stay in memory.
Reopen the Terminal; the tab is back with those edits.

examples.situation: A script is longer than the rows that fit and the cursor moves past the last visible row.
examples.whatHappens: The rows scroll to keep the cursor in view.
The panel shows blank rows with only the red and + buttons, and typing does nothing.

examples.situation: A script with a parse error is saved.
examples.whatHappens: The file is written, as today, and the error shows in the dark top strip.

leftOut: New syntax colors beyond black plain text; to be tweaked later.
Deleting script files from the Terminal.
Switching to font.ttf; text stays in the original font.

decisions.decision: The Terminal is 128x96 reference pixels, scaled up; the drawn 120x87 mock-up is resized to match the labels.
A new - button closes the currently selected file.
The + button creates a new script.
Text stays in the original font, the SDL debug font.
The red button closes the Terminal, same as Esc. The red, - and + buttons sit in their bright look and go dim while hovered.
The - button closes the tab only; the file stays on disk and its tab returns the next time the Terminal opens.
Text is smaller than the art: art and text scale separately, so a row holds about 45 characters.
Plain text changes from white to black; every other text color stays as it is for now, to be tweaked later.
The panel shows about 6 rows of 12 reference pixels and scrolls through longer scripts with the wheel and the cursor.
Saved and parse error messages show in the dark top strip, as light text.
The + button opens a new tab with an editable name; Enter creates the .txt file, Esc cancels.
Tabs widen to fit their names, and squeeze down when the bar fills up.
The panel uses the largest whole-number scale that fits inside 80% of the window, centered.
Unsaved edits stay in memory when the - button closes a tab, and are back when the tab returns.
After the last tab closes, the panel shows blank rows with only the red and + buttons; typing does nothing.
The autocomplete popup keeps its current look; the user will add its new look later.
Replaces D-9: the dash-dot dividers are gone and rows are tight, one glyph plus 2 text pixels tall, so as many rows as fit show and longer scripts still scroll.
decisions.reason: The user asked to delete the dividing line and shrink the gaps after seeing the build.

decisions.decision: The red button moves into the left corner of a 5 pixel top strip with no navy tile, tabs start at the panel's left edge, and a 2 pixel light band sits under the tab bar.
Replaces D-17's row height: rows are 4 reference pixels tall, from 2 pixels below the light band; the dashed mark in the reference is a height guide and is not drawn.
decisions.reason: The user updated the reference and confirmed the mark is a guide.

decisions.decision: Both scrollbars work, by wheel and thumb drag, are hidden by default, and resize their thumbs with the file.
Replaces D-1's fixed size: the Terminal panel is resizable by dragging its edges; 128x96 is its starting size. 'Window' here means the Terminal panel, since the game runs fullscreen.
Dragging the dark top strip moves the Terminal panel, keeping it fully on screen.
Replaces D-19's row height: the gap between rows is half of what a 4 reference pixel row leaves.
decisions.reason: The user found the space too big and asked for half size.

decisions.decision: In script rows, a space after a line's first word is half a character wide; indent spaces stay full width so blocks line up.
decisions.reason: The user found the space between words too big and asked for half size.

decisions.decision: Replaces D-5's hover for - and +, which now have one white look; only the red button dims on hover. The tab bar is 7 pixels tall with 3 white rows, the - and + glyphs are 3 pixels wide, the red square has a darker center, rows start 4 pixels below the band, and the vertical thumb is inset 4 pixels at its top.
Replaces D-16: the autocomplete list follows the reference, with a navy edge, a light top band and a white body. The picked row uses light grey, which the reference does not show.
decisions.reason: The user added the list to the reference.

decisions.decision: Replaces D-26's top band: the autocomplete list has no shadow row, only a navy edge and a white body.
decisions.reason: The user deleted the shadow in the reference.

decisions.decision: Replaces D-25's single look for - and +: their glyphs are white at rest and light grey #d9d9d9 while hovered.
decisions.reason: The user added the hover looks to the reference.

decisions.decision: A Terminal icon button sits at the left of the game screen, 25% from the top, with a gap from the left edge, and a click opens the Terminal.

assumptions.statement: Shift+1 still opens the Terminal alongside the button, Esc still closes it, and saving, autocomplete and the parse check keep working.
